task.text: Clients talk to one gateway; the gateway authenticates, routes and combines.
Implement `Gateway` in `Gateway.java`. `Request`, `Response` and `Service` are given and must not change.

items: `new Gateway(Set<String> tokens)`; `route(prefix, service)` and `aggregate(path, prefixes)` return the gateway so calls chain.
`handle(request)`: a token that is null or not allowed gives `401 "unauthorized"`, before anything else.
An aggregate path calls each listed route and joins the bodies with `" | "`, in order, as `200`. A route that throws, answers 5xx or does not exist contributes `<prefix>:n/a`.
Otherwise forward to the route with the **longest** matching prefix, whatever the order of registration. No match gives `404 "no route"`.

checks.title: The service sees the original request
The longest prefix wins in any order
Bad tokens never reach a service
An aggregate joins its parts in order
A failing part degrades to n/a

hints.text: Routes are data: a table from prefix to service. Authentication happens once, at the door, before any lookup. What decides between two prefixes that both match?

Keep a `Map<String, Service>` for routes and a `Map<String, List<String>>` for aggregates. In `handle`: check the token, look for an aggregate by exact path, else scan prefixes keeping the longest match.
